Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818)
937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is
discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance,
please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5.  CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Kassakhian attended the International Children’s Day Festival at Verdugo
  Park. He congratulated the organizers for a successful event. He attended the Glendale
  High School graduation and was impressed by the graduates.

  Mayor Brotman announced that the City of Glendale is now part of the City Data Alliance
  Accelerator Program. A group called Bloomberg Center for Government of Excellence ©
  (GovEx) organized a meeting here in Glendale and city staff and GovEx agreed on a vision
  statement which Brotman will share in two weeks.

  City Manager Roubik Golanian announced there will be a “Council in Your Neighborhood”
  meeting next week on June 20, 6pm at Pacific Community Center. Items for discussion will
  _ be Council Districting, Summer Programs, and Public Arts updates.

  Councilmember Najarian announced that this Friday will be the opening of the new Metro
  Regional Connector Subway line which ties all rail lines through Downtown Los Angeles.
  The Metro Rail System is offering free rides this Friday to Sunday. Najarian stated that the
  US Federal Government will issue a grant for $38.3M going towards the San Fernando and
  Doran Street rail crossing. He also stated that funds will roll in for the Glendale Beeline Plan
  which will be used for operations, electrification, and improvement of building structures.
  Najarian attended the International Transit Conference last week where discussions were
  held about zero-emission vehicles, equity, and environmental justices throughout the world.

  Councilmember Najarian read his statement on the protest that happened last Tuesday at
  the Glendale Unified School Board meeting. Mayor Brotman thanked the Glendale Police
  Department for keeping the community safe especially during the protest. Councilmember
  Asatryan condemned the extremist outside agitators and groups including Antifa and the
  Proud Boys who ventured into the City of Glendale with the intent to disrupt and instigate
  violence. She went on to confirm, following discussion with Glendale Police Chief Manny
  Cid, that these outside groups did come in and none of the arrests made included Glendale
  parents, a fact she wants widely recognized and acknowledged. She emphasized that it's
  every citizen's right, parents included, to voice their concerns and opinions without fear.
  Furthermore, she noted, it is the duty of leaders to establish and maintain an environment
  safe for such discourse in a civil manner. Addressing the recent wave of hate crimes in the
  city that have targeted various communities including the Armenian, LGBTQ+, and Jewish
  populations, Councilmember Asatryan underscored that the Armenian community continues
  to be a specific target of hate.
